title: What Are the Standards of Good Agricultural Practices in Bangladesh?
content:
The standards of Good Agricultural Practices in Bangladesh include:
1. Safe fruits and vegetables
2. Quality products
3. Environmental management
4. Workers' health, safety, and welfare.

title: What Are the Four Main Pillars of Good Agricultural Practices?
content:
The four main pillars of Good Agricultural Practices are:
1. Food safety and improved quality
2. Economic sustainability
3. Environmental sustainability
4. Social acceptability.

title: What Needs to Be Done While Following Good Agricultural Practices?
content:
While following Good Agricultural Practices:
- Crops should be cultivated after testing the soil and irrigation water.
- Organic fertilizers and organic pesticides should be used.
- Measures must be taken to keep crops free from contamination during and after harvesting.
- These practices ensure that the produced fruits and vegetables are safe for consumers' health.

title: Responsibilities of GAP Farmers
content:
GAP farmers have the following responsibilities:
• Know and follow all rules, protocols, regulations, laws, and guidelines of Good Agricultural Practices.
• Apply GAP rules to selected GAC partner crops to ensure safe and nutritious food production while protecting the environment, ensuring social responsibility, and maintaining farm worker health and safety.
• Be aware of the history and condition of the selected land and surrounding areas.
• Test soil and water before cultivation; apply fertilizers based on test results and advice from trained personnel. Give priority to organic fertilizers.
• Use pollution-free and safe water for irrigation and cleaning harvested crops.
• Apply only approved pesticides at the correct dose, timing, and method, prioritizing organic pesticides.
• Maintain a clean farm environment with proper sanitation and waste management.
• Ensure a first-aid box, toilet facilities, and safe drinking water are available on the farm.
• Harvest crops at the correct time and following the maturity index.
• Apply environmentally friendly pest control methods; use government-approved pesticides as a last resort and observe waiting periods.
• Ensure all processing materials, places, and water are contamination-free after harvesting; follow processing guidelines.
• Clean, sort, grade, and pack products properly after harvesting.
• Maintain personal hygiene and strengthen farm biosecurity before and after work.
• Clean and store tools, machinery, and equipment properly after farm work.
• Record all farm management and cultivation activities in the GAC farmer register or logbook, and have them audited.
• Obtain GAP certification to market produced products properly.
• Seek advice from locally trained GAC agricultural officers and partner officials for proper GAP crop cultivation and marketing.
